To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD34+ cell adhesiveness differs between patients mobilized using chemotherapy plus granulocyte–colonystimulating factor (G‐CSF) versus G‐CSF alone.

the expression of adhesion molecule profiles differs between patients mobilized using granulocyte–macrophage colony‐stimulating factor (GM‐CSF) or chemotherapy followed by GM‐CSF and that the adhesion molecule profiles of mobilized CD34+ cells from patients mobilized with chemotherapy followed by GM-CSF are similar to those from normal bone marrow (BM).

CD34+ cell adhesin molecule profiles differ between GCSF alone and chemotherapy followed GCSF mobilized patients and that CD34+ cell expression of L-selectin and CD62L was significantly lower in patients mobilized with chemotherapy plus GCSF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of adhesion molecules in the mobilization of CD34+ cells.
the study of the adhesion molecule profiles of CD34+ cells from normal donors and patients with lymphoma or myeloma.
the role of adhesion molecules in the mobilization of CD34+ cells from the bone marrow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a lack of evidence to support the use of prophylactic platelet transfusions to reduce the risk of bleeding in patients with thrombocytopenia.
the use of chemotherapy followed by G‐CSF mobilization results in greater down regulation of adhesion molecules and a greater mobilization of CD34+ cells.

the use of chemotherapy plus G-CSF for CD34+ cell collection is associated with a more profound downregulation of CD34+ adhesion molecules, which is consistent with the observation of a superior mobilization of CD34+ cells with the combination of chemotherapy and growth factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CD34+ cells mobilized with G-CSF alone are not as differentiated as those mobilized with chemotherapy followed by G-CSF, and that CD34+ cell differentiation may be a factor in the mobilization and collection of CD34+ cells.

the adhesion molecule profiles of CD34+ cells are different between mobilization strategies, with greater down regulations of adhesion molecules observed with chemotherapy plus growth factor mobilization.

the adhesion molecule profile of CD34+ cells differs between patients mobilized by chemotherapy and growth factors compared with patients mobilized by growth factors alone, and that these differences may contribute to the superior CD34+ cell collection in the former group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adhesion molecule expression profile is significantly different between patients mobilized by chemotherapy and growth factors compared with patients mobilized by growth factors alone.
the CD34+ cell adhesin profile is altered in the mobilized blood of patients who have received chemotherapy plus G-CSF compared to G-CSF alone.
the CD34+ cell adhesin molecule profiles differ between G-CSF and chemo-G-CSF mobilization.
